function: system (p. 2): DDPG power allocation over HARQ-IR rounds in ISAC, area 5, on a single-antenna link: CU 'equipped with a single antenna', scalar channel hSU,k, no RIS.
notes: Title on p. 1 ('Throughput Maximization of HARQ-IR for ISAC') and the DOI printed there match the work. Step 1: a research letter that proposes a GP-based and a DRL-based (DDPG) power allocation across HARQ-IR rounds; the learned DDPG policy sets the transmit power of each round, a physical-layer resource that serves both communication (LTAT objective, outage constraint) and sensing (probability-of-detection constraint (8d)), so checks 3 to 5 pass as area 5 (ISAC). Check 6 applies: p. 2 states 'the CU is equipped with a single antenna and the BS is equipped with separate transmit and receive antennas for simultaneous ISAC signal transmission and radar echo reception', i.e. one transmit and one receive antenna; the channels hSU,k ~ CN(0,1), hST,k and hTS,k are scalar Rayleigh coefficients (eqs. 1-2, gamma_c,k = Pk|hSU,k|^2/sigma_c^2), with no precoder, no beams, and no RIS. Area 5 does not admit single-antenna links, so the reason is system. For the reviewer: power allocation across HARQ rounds could also be read as link adaptation (check 5, function); I kept area 5 because the allocated power also serves the sensing constraint. The work does report numerical results (Figs. 2-4, pp. 4-5), so check 7 would not apply.
